taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Bothriochloa barbinodis at species rank and folds named varieties such as var. barbinodis into the species-level concept used by this learner.
look_here_first: CANE BLUESTEM: find a true stem NODE with a dense ring or beard of soft white hairs, then follow its many branched, silvery terminal racemes into a relatively broad FAN-shaped head. Never identify from white fluff alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Williamson County — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed field-based treatment of Bothriochloa barbinodis. Val Verde County — the Amistad National Recreation Area vascular flora documents cane bluestem on rocky slopes and flats; USDA/Native Plants release data also include a Val Verde collection. Uvalde County — Texas Native Seeds/USDA collection data include a Bothriochloa barbinodis accession collected on Highway 55 south of the campground in Uvalde County.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: County PASS uses explicit county field/specimen/collection records. Broad Edwards Plateau or South Texas distribution is supporting context only.

best_field_traits: Perennial bunchgrass with robust stems, often bent at the base.
Check stem nodes: densely bearded with conspicuous soft white hairs, commonly several millimeters long; Texas A&M reports hairs up to 12.5 mm.
Flowering head usually 5–14 cm long, dense and silvery with many branches, often broad or fan-shaped.
Branchlets bear paired spikelets with bent or twisted awns; need magnified same-plant study.
Distinguish from KR's several relatively narrow exposed terminal fingers and from silver bluestem's contracted narrow cottony head.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: FIRST CHECK THE NODE: cane = heavy white beard, silver = pale usually smooth, KR = hairs variable but not a comparable heavy beard. THEN check head: cane = many relatively long branches making a fan; silver = numerous SHORT closely compressed cottony branches; KR = several slender LONG fingers.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Cane bluestem: true culm nodes bear a conspicuous beard of long soft hairs, with a relatively broad fan-shaped silvery inflorescence. Silver bluestem: contracted narrow woolly head with numerous shorter rames, usually pale smooth nodes. KR bluestem: generally several long thin radiating racemes in one terminal head; short node hairiness can vary so absence/presence of tiny hairs is not decisive. Little bluestem: separate short silky racemes repeatedly positioned along the upper leafy culm.

field_id_finish_pass.priority: Avoid removal of native cane bluestem as assumed KR; identify true nodes before management.
crew_sequence: Photograph rooted whole plant, flowering head and at least two actual culm nodes on the SAME stem.
At a joint where the leaf sheath emerges, look for a dense halo/beard of long soft hairs; do not mistake an inflorescence branch for a node.
Trace the many head branches to see a broadly spreading or fanlike outline; note that immature heads may look narrow.
Magnify an attached mature branch with its sessile and pedicelled spikelets and bent awns.
Before assigning an invasive status, compare KR, silver bluestem, little bluestem and bushy bluestem; uncertain specimens remain Bothriochloa sp.

locally_useful_distinctions.cue: Several LONG thin fingerlike racemes in a terminal cluster; stiff papilla-based hairs on upper leaf blade near collar support ID
MANY SHORT silky racemes occur separately on branching upper leafy stems; often a tight clump
Usually 2–6 relatively STOUT exposed racemes near one terminal point, often turkey-foot
Dense broad BRUSH of crowded short silky paired racemes, subtended by spathe-like leafy sheaths
Narrow contracted COTTONY SILVER head of >10 short rames; pale usually smooth nodes
Single narrow-to-open golden BRANCHED PANICLE and conspicuous pointed membranous 'rifle-sight' ligule
Relatively narrow silky inflorescence of paired rames partly held in long flattened spathe-like sheaths

photo_targets: Hays/target-region, specimen-verified hairy true culm NODE close-up with ruler and sheath junction, ideally two nodes.
Same rooted flowering cane bluestem showing complete fan-shaped panicle and true lower stem.
Full branch and mature sessile/pedicelled spikelets with 1-mm ruler.
Field matched KR, silver and cane flowering stems at the same stage.

visual_comparison.overlay_note: TRUE measured node beards are in appended Texas images. The upper hair-fringed SHEATH edge is NOT the CULM node and is NOT a measured free ligule. A whole awned reproductive unit does not prove individual glume, lemma or sessile/pedicelled assignments.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — BEARDED STEM NODE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Find the conspicuous pale hair beard on a TRUE culm joint, then trace the same stem to a many-branched silvery head.
field_id_short_tiles.details: First find a genuine CULM node, NOT the base of a leaf blade or a fluffy flowering rachis. New real cane photos 5 and 6 show thick rings of long ascending soft hairs at true stem joints on a research-grade Williamson County plant. Photo 5 has a millimeter ruler beside two photographed nodes. Then compare the broader silvery head to KR and silver. Published hair-length ranges remain source claims, not independent direct measurements from the ruler pixels.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ACTUAL TRUE BEARDED CULM NODES PHOTO-VERIFIED WITH RULER

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · ROOTED PERENNIAL AND TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Warm-season bunchgrass; culms usually 60–120 cm; TRUE membranous ligule approximately 1–2 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: See panels 7–8 for an OUTER blade–sheath junction and a distinct hairy upper sheath margin; neither proves an exposed free inner membranous ligule. Panel 10 shows a living bunch above soil with roots hidden. The actual true CULM nodes with a physical millimeter ruler are on panel 5, not on the collars. A peeled-open 1–3 mm inner ligule and genuinely excavated connected fibrous roots are still missing.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PARTIAL PHOTO EVIDENCE — actual node/collar/aboveground bunch; free inner ligule and roots absent

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · MANY RACEMES, TWO SPIKELETS PER PAIR
field_id_short_tiles.short: Silvery panicle approximately 5–14 cm; numerous branches; sessile fertile and smaller pedicelled companion spikelets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Texas A&M describes a dense often fanlike panicle; USFS gives individual racemes about 2–7 cm. On a mature branch identify the larger sessile fertile spikelet and the stalked smaller usually sterile or male companion. A source-identified paired-spikelet JPEG is recorded, but lacks calibrated local dissection. Do not arrow a whole raceme as a single spikelet.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL SOURCE PHOTO — SCALED PAIR STILL MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · GLUMES, LEMMA AND TWISTED AWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Sessile spikelet about 4.5–7.3 mm; two firm glumes, one lower sterile floret, one upper fertile floret; awn 20–35 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Separate both glumes from a ripe sessile spikelet. The lower glume may have a dorsal pit OR no pit, so absence does not exclude cane. Within the glumes, the slender upper fertile LEMMA bears the long knee-bent, twisted AWN, not the glume. Record individual glume length and the real awn insertion with a 1-mm ruler before making microscopic arrows.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED TRAIT — MEASURED LOCAL ANATOMY PENDING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · CANE VS INVASIVE KR AND SILVER BLUESTEM
field_id_short_tiles.short: Cane: conspicuously bearded true nodes and many silvery fanlike branches; KR: more fingerlike branches and different paired spikelet proportions.
field_id_short_tiles.details: PHOTO COMPARISON NOW PRESENT: panel 0 is actual CANE paired silky flowering head, panel 2 is introduced TEXAS KR bluestem (Tyler Cannon CC BY 4.0) with typically longer more fingerlike branches, and panel 3 is native SILVER bluestem (Matt Lavin CC BY-SA 2.0) with dense cottony shorter rames. Those panels are different source-matched species and their own archived local files; no borrowing as cane anatomy. The critically conspicuous bearded TRUE cane CULM node, actual short inner MEMBRANOUS ligule and fully measured sessile/pedicelled pair are STILL missing. Do not authorize removal using flowering architecture alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TWO LICENSED EXACT LOOK-ALIKE PHOTOS INSTALLED IN GALLERY — REAL NODE/INNER LIGULE PENDING

Existing specimen/source archived media remains preserved, and KR/silver photos are labeled as OTHER species. grass_species_finalization_20261026.look_here_first: On a true stem joint find a conspicuous white/tan beard; trace the same rooted plant to a many-branched silvery fanlike head. Confirm the paired sessile/pedicelled spikelets before distinguishing from KR and silver bluestem.

measured_diagnostic_key.growth: Warm-season perennial bunchgrass, culms usually 60–120 cm; true node hairs commonly 3–4 mm (sometimes longer).
measured_diagnostic_key.ligule_collar: Membranous ligule about 1–2 mm, often erose; measure blade–sheath junction, not node beard.
measured_diagnostic_key.panicle: Dense silvery panicle about 5–14 cm, many branches, individual racemes about 2–7 cm.
measured_diagnostic_key.spikelets: Sessile fertile spikelets 4.5–7.3 mm, paired with smaller/narrower pedicelled male or sterile spikelets.
measured_diagnostic_key.glumes: Two firm glumes on sessile spikelet; lower may or may not have dorsal pit.
measured_diagnostic_key.lemma_awn: Lower sterile and upper fertile florets; fertile lemma carries twisted geniculate awn about 20–35 mm.
measured_diagnostic_key.lookalikes: KR Bothriochloa ischaemum, silver B. torreyana, Schizachyrium scoparium, Anatherum glomeratum; node + panicle + mature spikelet proportions required.

beginner_learning_path.title: Cane bluestem — seven real photos, find the bearded NODE before removing a grass
beginner_learning_path.intro: Follow real cane-bluestem photographs from the whole flowering head to actual Texas bearded CULM nodes (one with a millimeter ruler), then compare an OUTER leaf collar and its hairy sheath edge, an awned flowering structure and invasive King Ranch. The free inner ligule and dug root crown remain unphotographed.
beginner_learning_path.memory_rule: CANE = conspicuous LONG pale beard of soft hairs at true stem NODES plus a broad silvery branching fan; do NOT confuse node hairs with white flowering-head hairs or with upper leaf-sheath hairs.

steps.title: 1 · Recognize the many-branched silvery head
steps.look_for: Silky long-awned flowering units cluster along multiple branching rames in John Rusk's source-confirmed cultivated cane bluestem.
steps.why_it_matters: Find the right family of grasses, but an individual fluffy head is not enough to authorize removal.

steps.title: 2 · Locate a living native Texas clump
steps.look_for: Inspect the attached aboveground culms and leaves in a natural rocky-soil stand from Brushy Creek, Williamson County. Roots are hidden.
steps.why_it_matters: An in-ground bunch is field context, not a photograph proving rhizome or fibrous root structure.

steps.title: 3 · FIND THE TRUE BEARDED NODE WITH MILLIMETER RULER
steps.look_for: Two real cane stem nodes have strong pale-white soft hair rings; the physical millimeter rule alongside is real. Follow each upright culm through the actual node.
steps.why_it_matters: This is cane bluestem's strongest distinguishing field trait versus invasive KR; do not mistake the separate flowering hair mass for a stem joint.

steps.title: 4 · Confirm the bearded node on a living stem
steps.look_for: Two separate actual flowering stalks have hairy white soft beard rings at TRUE nodes, not where leaves arise from a sheath.
steps.why_it_matters: This makes the key feature recognizable without a ruler and shows natural variation in the beard.

steps.title: 5 · See the OUTER leaf collar, not an opened ligule
steps.look_for: A leaf blade emerges from the green wrapping sheath. No free membranous inner ligule rim is separately exposed in this image.
steps.why_it_matters: The blade–sheath collar is not the same structure as a bearded culm node. Open the INNER sheath for a proper ligule photo.

steps.title: 6 · Identify an awned reproductive unit next to a ruler
steps.look_for: See pale silky hairs, an elongated flowering unit and awns with real ruler markings; distinguish fine white hairs from longer firm awns.
steps.why_it_matters: A true dissected attached fertile sessile/pedicelled pair and lemma awn insertion still require closer images.

steps.title: 7 · Rule out invasive King Ranch bluestem
steps.look_for: This is real Texas KR, not cane. See fewer relatively long terminal fingerlike racemes, compared with cane's denser fan and its long-bearded culm nodes.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm cane at two true nodes before vegetation removal. When unsure, retain native candidates until diagnostic anatomy is checked.

beginner_learning_path.safety_note: Photograph two true stem nodes and a mature head before removing a suspected invasive; if they cannot be seen, label Bothriochloa sp. Pending: actual peeled-open INNER 1–3 mm ligule with ruler, a dug root/rhizome crown, and a source-verified connected mature sessile/pedicelled spikelet pair. The licensed photographed cane belongs to an identified Williamson County specimen, not a documented Hays collection.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Cane bluestem — fast crew recognition with real source photos
steps: 1 · First inspect the TRUE stem NODES: cane has unusually conspicuous long pale soft HAIR BEARDS (our Texas photo 5 includes a ruler).
2 · Find the SILVERY HEAD: numerous racemes in a broadly branched fan; fluffy flower hairs alone do not diagnose cane.
3 · Compare the outer leaf collar with the actual node: photo 7 is the OUTER blade–sheath junction; photo 8 shows a hairy sheath rim, neither an exposed inner free ligule.
4 · Examine mature awned spikelets, but do not label a sterile pedicelled partner or lemma insertion unless an intact connected pair is photographed and measured.
5 · Compare source-verified silver and introduced KR photographs. If the node is obscured, do NOT remove a possible native cane based on seedhead alone.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Actual cane true bearded nodes are now photographed at ruler scale; inner free ligule and exposed roots are NOT. Noncommercial CC BY-NC per-image terms and source attribution must remain visible.
